tool.name: FAIRe mapper: find primers
tool.description: look up primer sequences from names, citations or methods text
tool.command: python '$__tool_directory__/faire_primers.py' #if $search.mode == 'text': text #for $t in $search.texts: '$t' #end for #else: lookup --queries_file '$queries' #if str($search.gene).strip(): --gene '$search.gene' #end if #end if #if $table.source != 'bundled': #import re #set $own_label = $re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9._ ()-]', '_', str($table.own.element_identifier)) --primers '$table.own' --primers_label '$own_label' #if $table.source == 'own': --no_bundled #end if #end if --output '$candidates'

param.name: mode
param.label: Look for primers in
param.option: A list of primer names, assay names or citations

param.name: texts
param.label: Methods text
param.help: Plain text, markdown or PDF. A PDF of scanned pages has no text to read: save Word files and scanned PDFs as text first.

param.name: names
param.label: Names or citations, one per line
param.help: For example MiFish-U-F, Bact16S_515F, teleo, or Pochon et al., 2013

param.name: gene
param.label: Only primers for this gene (optional)
param.help: 12S, 16S, 18S, COI, CytB ... or a FAIRe target_gene value such as 12S rRNA (SSU mitochondria)

param.name: source
param.label: Primer table
param.option: The table that comes with the tool
The table that comes with the tool, plus my own

param.name: own
param.label: My primer table
param.help: A table made by FAIRe mapper: build primer table, or a TSV with the same columns. Its rows replace bundled rows with the same sequences.

has_line_matching.expression: ^TAReuk454FWD1; CCAGCASCYGCGGTAATTCC / ACTTTCGTTCTTGATYRATGA\tsequences in the text\t\d+\t.*\t18S V4 \(Australian Microbiome\)\t.*
^ACGTGGTCAGGATCCAAGTT / TTGCAGGATCCTTAGCACGA\tsequences in the text \(not in the primer table\)\t.*\t12S rRNA \(SSU mitochondria\)\t\tLab12S-F\tACGTGGTCAGGATCCAAGTT\t\tLab12S-R\t.*

tool.help:
@EARLY_VERSION@ **What it does**
FAIRe needs the primer sequences (``pcr_primer_forward`` and ``pcr_primer_reverse``), but methods sections often give only a name ("the MiFish primer set", "Bact16S_515F") or a citation ("universal eukaryote 18S assay (Pochon et al., 2013)"). This tool looks up the primer pairs that those names and citations point to in a primer table, so you can check them and copy the sequences. When the methods give the sequences themselves, the tool reads those too, and names the pair from the table if the sequences match one.
The tool never chooses between candidates, because names such as 515F or 806R are used for several different sequences. Check each candidate against the original paper before you use it.
-----
**Inputs**
- **Methods or README text**, as plain text, markdown or a PDF. A PDF of scanned pages holds images of the text, which the tool can't read: save it, or a Word file, as text first. The tool looks for primer and assay names, including names inside longer names, such as *Bact16S_515F* or a file name containing *teleo*. It also looks for citations of a primer's authors, but counts these only when the same sentence names the primers' gene.
The tool also reads primer sequences written in the text: 15 to 45 IUPAC letters in capitals, such as ``TAReuk454FWD1 (CCAGCASCYGCGGTAATTCC)``, or two sequences in a table row. Two sequences in one sentence or row are taken as a pair, forward first. Text copied from a PDF table often has the sequences on rows of their own, out of order and sometimes broken across lines. The tool pairs these when they are the two primers of a pair in the primer table, or when one is named as a forward primer (…F, Fwd) and the next as a reverse primer (…R, Rev). Any sequences left over are listed one by one. Illumina adapters and overhangs are left out.
A pair whose sequences are in the primer table is shown with the table's names and references. A pair that is not in the table is shown as written, with the name before each sequence and the gene named on the same line. - **Or a list** of primer names, assay names or citations, one per line. - **Primer table**: the table that comes with the tool (described below), your own table, or both. You can make your own with **FAIRe mapper: build primer table**.
**Output**
The output has one row for each candidate primer pair. It shows what matched (the words in the text, or the name you gave), how it matched (sequences in the text, name, part of a name, reference, or author and gene), the number of candidates, and the pair's names, sequences, references, target gene and source row. Pairs whose sequences are in the text come first.
-----
**The bundled primer table**
The primer table that comes with the tool is built from three sources: the metabarcoding and species-specific primer tables (Tables S3 and S4) of Takahashi et al. 2023, *Aquatic environmental DNA: a review of the macro-organismal biomonitoring revolution*, Science of the Total Environment 873:162322 (CC BY-NC 4.0); a metazoan primer register that puts those tables in FAIRe terms, adding the target taxon and the gene in the FAIRe vocabulary; and a register of bacteria and archaea 16S primer pairs (the pairs recommended by Klindworth et al. 2013, the Earth Microbiome Project primers, and other common pairs). The columns use FAIRe term names, so values such as ``targetTaxonomicAssay`` and ``target_gene`` can be copied straight into a FAIRe workbook. Each row records its source.
